filename: A Long-term Consistent Artificial Intelligence and Remote Sensing-based Soil Moisture Dataset_.pdf
title: A Long-term Consistent Artificial Intelligence and Remote Sensing-based Soil Moisture Dataset
code_availability: All code is written in Python, the analysis is conducted using Columbia University high performance computing clusters (Ginsburg), and is available at https://github.com/os2328/CASM-dataset.
testbed_rationale: CASM is an observational remote-sensing derived product harmonizing topsoil moisture across multiple satellites, intended for climate monitoring, water cycle analysis, or data assimilation rather than serving directly as a training/evaluation benchmark testbed for ML parameterizations or physics emulators.
pain_points: Satellite swath timing and orbit differences prevent complete global daily overlap across multiple sensors, necessitating 3-day temporal binning.

The strong periodic annual seasonal cycle dominates raw microwave brightness temperatures and soil moisture, causing unadjusted neural networks to fit seasonality well while failing on extreme anomalies.
Discrepancies in instrument characteristics (frequencies, incidence angles, RF interference) introduce artificial decadal trends and offsets when blending heterogeneous satellite missions.
Separating epistemic (structural) from aleatoric (input noise) uncertainty in neural networks requires computationally intensive deep ensembling and input perturbations.
extraction_notes: The work was developed under the NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (award #2019625). Deseasonalization is carried out via gridpoint-specific sinusoidal fits before neural network training to ensure fidelity in predicting SM extremes.
